STEP 1 - Scene: A top-down photo of a few olives on a white square plate, with a paper sheet and QR codes underneath.

STEP 2 - Ruler: The plate is a square side plate about 22 cm across, so its area is roughly 22 × 22 ≈ 450 cm² (corners are rounded, call it ~420 cm²).

STEP 3 - Items: Dark olives, probably Kalamata-type, pitted or not. I count 10: 9 purple-brown and 1 blacker one.

STEP 4 - Area: Each olive is about 3 cm long and 1.8 cm wide, so it covers ~4 cm² from above. Ten olives cover ~40 cm², which is about 9% of the plate. The sum of items matches this.

STEP 5 - Volume: Each olive is an ellipsoid of about 3 × 1.8 × 1.8 cm, so its volume is 0.52 × 3 × 1.8 × 1.8 ≈ 5 ml. Ten olives come to ~50 ml.

STEP 6 - Grams: Olives are dense, about 1.0 g/ml, which gives ~50 g. Kalamata olives with pits weigh about 4–5 g each, so ~45 g for 10 is consistent. I'll use 45 g.

STEP 7 - Energy: Kalamata olives are about 115–140 kcal/100 g, so I'll use 130. 45 g × 1.3 ≈ 59 kcal.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: Ten olives weighing about 45 g and giving about 60 kcal is plausible.
